title: Time Series Atlas
question: Which time series methods answer useful questions once source conventions, information timing, and evaluation assumptions are made explicit?
one_liner: Forecasting and detection studies with a visible record of the questions, critiques, and corrections behind each result.
aim: Demonstrate analytical judgment through reproducible investigations and short process stories, with independent agent reviews before design, execution, and publication.
scope: Completed atmospheric carbon dioxide and electricity forecasting studies plus a known-truth change-detection experiment. Retail, oil, river flow, air quality, and ECG studies remain planned.
conclusion: Recent-growth forecasts improved the declared carbon dioxide comparison. Sharing electricity-model coefficients generally did not help this panel. Persistent noise broke the detector's calibrated false-alert behavior.

summary.question: What changes when we challenge the question, measurements, and evaluation before trusting a time series result?
summary.result: The first studies show why shared information, more history, and fast detection are not automatically improvements.

finding: In the fixed electricity panel, the shared model worsened forecasts for {{test.pooled_worse_customers:d}} customers. Separate models also had the lower aggregate-load error; the few customer gains from sharing were small.

For three-year December targets, adapting to recent growth reduced carbon dioxide MAE from {{co2_fixed:.3f}} ppm to {{co2_recent:.3f}} ppm. These are revised-data hindcasts, not all-month or causal claims.
In the synthetic control, persistent noise sharply increased false alerts under a frozen threshold. Conditional detection delay alone hid that failure.

The process story preserves source/documentation discrepancies, actual scoring defects found before full runs, original agent critiques, and verified corrections. Agent agreement is not independent human validation.

traps.how: Features use only observations available at each declared origin; future-perturbation checks test that earlier predictions remain unchanged.
Power and interval labels are explicit. Provider DST conventions differ from sampled values, so calendar masks and a nominal-clock assumption are recorded.
Comparison designs were committed before fitting, with no model selection on final scores. Customer differences and sensitivity results remain visible.

figures.caption: Customer-level gains and losses from sharing regression coefficients, with aggregate error scored after summing the panel.
December-origin forecast errors and paired differences against the expanding fixed-growth baseline.
A frozen detector threshold behaves differently under independent and persistent synthetic noise. Detection rates are conditional on no early alarm.

not_claimed: Universal model rankings, causal attribution, realized savings, or clinical benefit.
A representative sample of all electricity customers or historical real-time data vintages.
Completion of the remaining planned studies or independent human validation.

verification.harness: Offline invariant tests; analysis evidence linked in each report

data: Pinned NOAA GML monthly carbon dioxide observations
